body:
Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on.").

Depends on #1860.

## Goal
Chain 2D sketch primitives within a caller tolerance in `crates/geometry/` into deterministic closed loops and open chains, classify outer loops vs holes, and enforce open-chain safety.

## Scope
- Take normalized 2D primitives (`Line`, `Arc`, `Circle`, `Polyline`) and layer names from #1860 together with a configurable join tolerance in millimeters (default `0.01` mm).
- Join touching endpoints that lie within the join tolerance into connected chains. Never bridge gaps wider than the tolerance.
- Keep original `Arc` and `Circle` segment metadata inside each chain so downstream CAM operations emit true `G2`/`G3` arcs where possible.
- Assign each chain a stable geometry-hash `ChainId` derived from its quantized curve geometry and layer name.
- Separate closed chains from open chains explicitly. Report open endpoints and never close an open chain silently.
- Resolve closed chain nesting into outer boundaries vs inner holes using `geo2d::Region` / `clipper2-rust` winding rules.
- Reject self-crossing closed loops and degenerate chains with clear named errors instead of panicking.
- Handle T-junctions or branching vertices cleanly with deterministic traversal or named diagnostics.

## Done means
Tests chain unordered lines, arcs, and circles into stable `ChainId` loops and open chains within a specified tolerance; gaps wider than tolerance remain explicitly open; nested rectangles and circles classify accurately as outer loops vs holes; self-crossing loops return a named error; arc metadata survives chaining.

Part of #1452
